logline: A terminally ill woman accidentally summons the personification of doom with a drunken wish, then signs a hundred-day contract with him - gambling her life against the world's annihilation in a romance built on borrowed time.

renewal.note: Single-season 16-episode run concluded June 29, 2021. Pre-sold to 150 countries; no sequel produced.

bollymeter.basis: Park Bo-young and Seo In-guk's chemistry is the engine - critics and audiences agreed it overcame a screenplay that leaned on cliches; IMDb settled at 7.8 and the show ranked on NME's best K-dramas of 2021 list.

seasons.review_body: Doom at Your Service aired on tvN from May to June 2021, averaging 3.027 percent nationwide cable ratings with a peak of 4.422 percent in episode two. The show was pre-sold to 150 countries and made available on Viki, Viu, and iQIYI, reflecting substantial international commercial positioning ahead of broadcast. NME placed it tenth on their best K-dramas of 2021 list. Critical conversation centred almost entirely on the lead pairing: Seo In-guk as a supernatural entity who delivers annihilation with deadpan menace, and Park Bo-young as a woman who refuses to be intimidated by her own death sentence. Detractors noted the screenplay relied on cliches and left emotional threads at a superficial level; defenders argued the leads transcended the writing. IMDb settled at 7.8, a solid placement for the genre.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the central contract - a dying woman summons doom and then refuses to behave like a victim - in a way that immediately separates the show from generic supernatural romance. Seo In-guk's entrance is calibrated for maximum unsettling charm and it works. The tone balances dark comedy and genuine pathos without collapsing either.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Dong-kyung's drunken curse lands - and doom materialises not as a monster but as a man with unreadable eyes.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the supernatural contract in a direction that divided audiences: those who found the ending earned and those who felt the resolution was too convenient given sixteen episodes of genuinely high stakes. The lead performances remain committed to the end and the emotional close lands on individual character beats even when the mythology frays.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment Myeolmang's choice becomes irrevocable - a scene that reframes the entire hundred-day premise.
